tytul: No-cook strawberry syrup for the refrigerator (Cocktail Contessa recipe)
wstep: This card follows the Cocktail Contessa recipe for no-cook strawberry syrup: strawberries and sugar stand in the refrigerator, then the syrup is strained and must be kept refrigerated. [T:ACI-754]

ostrzezenia.tekst: This syrup is never heated: NCHFP warns that uncooked jams mold or ferment in a short time at room temperature, so keep the fruit and the syrup in the refrigerator at every step. [T:SLO-020,ACI-754]

akapity: The source is a drinks recipe, not a tested preserving recipe, so JarAtlas uses the shorter storage time it gives. [T:ACI-754]
The US FDA list gives strawberries an approximate pH of 3.00–3.90. [T:ACI-136]
Strawberries and sugar in a ratio of 2 : 1 by weight, that is twice as much fruit as sugar. [T:ACI-754]
Sort and wash fully ripe berries, drain them and remove the caps and stems, as NCHFP directs for uncooked berry jam. [T:SLO-309]
Put the strawberries and sugar in a clean jar and leave it in the refrigerator for 12–24 hours. [T:ACI-754]
Sterilize canning jars and prepare two-piece canning lids according to the manufacturer’s directions. [T:SLO-309]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): pour the strained syrup into a jar sterilized this way, close it and put it back in the refrigerator. [T:SLO-309,ACI-754]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): use the syrup within 10 days and throw away what is left; the source gives about 10–12 days in the refrigerator, and JarAtlas takes the shorter number. [T:ACI-754]

JarAtlas rule (cautious): NCHFP says an opened container of uncooked jam should be kept in the refrigerator and used within a few days; treat an opened jar of this uncooked syrup the same way. [T:SLO-460]

JarAtlas rule (cautious): keep the jar on the middle shelf of the refrigerator, not in the door: Wisconsin Extension assumes 40 °F (4.4 °C) or colder for refrigerator pickles, while a Polish sanitary inspection office gives about 10 °C for the door, even though it suggests the door for jars of preserves. [T:ACI-523]
